text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 00:12 UTC — elevated 5xx rate for model ruma-v3 (quant) in eu-west1. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6.8% over 5m. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/alerts/2391234567

sre-oncall: ack. I'm on it. Paging primary SRE and ML oncall. @matt @sophie

matt: oncall here, looking now. Any customer-facing errors reported?

sre-oncall: some API keys show spike in 5xx + decode errors in logs: "kv-cache-miss overflow" across multiple hosts. Latency p95 also up.

sophie: adding context — ruma-v3 is the quantized experimental variant we rolled yesterday to 10% traffic. Stable model is ruma-stable-2.

irene: if this is kv-cache overflow, quick path is to stop feeding new requests to ruma-v3 and shift to stable. Also consider keywise throttles for heavy customers.

sre-oncall: proposed mitigations — 1) drain and disable ruma-v3 in eu-west1, 2) apply temporary key-slice quotas to heavy keys, 3) route 100% to ruma-stable-2 in-region. Any objections?

matt: +1. I'll execute. Running `routing disable-variant` then `quota slice`.

deploy-bot: running preflight checks: `canary-check` ... ok.

sre-oncall: executing now. Paste of commands/logs as I run them:

```
# disable ruma-v3 for serving in eu-west1 (graceful drain)
redwoodctl routing update --variant ruma-v3 --region eu-west1 --action disable --drain
```

deploy-bot: command accepted. Drain in progress. Estimated time to zero in-flight: ~45s.

sre-oncall: next step — apply key-slice quotas for heavy keys:

```
# apply keywise slice for customer keys >100r/s
redwoodctl quota set --key-filter "customer:enterprise_*" --max-rps 50 --window 60s --note "temp slice due to ruma-v3 errors"
```

ops-lead: add emergency notice for CS: "temporary limits, monitoring 30m, will re-evaluate".

matt: shifting traffic now to stable:

```
redwoodctl routing set-weight --source all --variant ruma-stable-2 --weight 100 --region eu-west1
```

sophie: monitoring: error rate on ruma endpoints is trending down after shift. p95 latency on ruma-stable-2 remains within SLO. Some heavy keys still show elevated latency (cold cache).

customer-success-bot: FYI — two customers opened tickets about slower responses earlier (tickets #13521, #13522). Not yet escalated.

irene: I'll push a temporary fallback that bypasses prefix cache for the heaviest keys to avoid cold-cache amplification while we monitor.

sre-oncall: drain finished — ruma-v3 instances at 0 in-flight. Marking variant state = suspended for eu-west1.

deploy-bot: state updated: ruma-v3 -> suspended.

matt: running smoke tests across a representative slice (10k requests over 2m) — all green.

sophie: proposal: keep ruma-v3 suspended until ML/infra reproduces and fixes kv-cache eviction interaction with quant weights. EM/PM notified. Recommend no re-enable tonight.

ops-lead: agreed. Assign ML infra owner to reproduce. Postmortem owner also assigned.

sre-oncall: customer impact summary: ~0.5% global requests affected by ruma-v3 traffic. Two customers reported transient slowness. No reported data loss. Incident ticket created: INC-2391.

matt: handing off to night oncall @irene. I'll update the incident doc with commands, timeline, and mitigation steps. If we see recurrence reopen pager. :thumbsup:

irene: ack — will monitor for re-queue spikes and anomalies. Can raise emergency quotas if required.

sophie: notes for postmortem: include exact UTC timeline, commands we ran, and tentative hypothesis (kv-cache eviction + quant model memory pattern). Also include steps for future: automated variant evacuation on kv-cache errors.

matt: closing active mitigation. Incident moved to MONITORING. If error returns, reopen pager. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status -> MONITORING. Active mitigation duration: ~12 minutes. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-variant-failure
